- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.4) — model is overly conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments after sentiment shifts to bearish, especially if sentiment drops sharply.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves: model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, leading to overprediction in the following days.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after strong upward moves, especially when sentiment is high and then drops.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising, then underestimate later days when sentiment stabilizes or turns neutral.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.7, reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for overconfidence; if sentiment < 0.3, increase forecast by 2–5% to capture hidden momentum.
